preamble: Fronting of the labio-velar glide /w/ to the palatal glide /j/ is well attested. Northwest Semitic changed Proto-Semitic word-initial *w- to *y- (Arabic walada vs Hebrew yālaḏ 'bore a child'); in eastern Modern West Frisian the rising diphthongs [wo] and [wa] after labials became [jo] and [ja] during the 20th century; and in the Arawakan language Trinitario /w/ regularly became /j/ before /p/.

examples.to: Hebrew yālaḏ, Aramaic yəlaḏ, Classical Syriac yəlaḏ
examples.note: Word-initial *w- became *y- in Northwest Semitic, while Arabic preserves w-.
Rising diphthong from New Frisian Breaking; the [j] onset occurs only after labial consonants.
Spread rapidly in the eastern Frisian-speaking area during the 20th century (mûljearring).
Change of w to j before p is regular in Trinitario (Ignaciano keeps -iwape).

sources: Dyk, S. (2011). Palatalization of the glide in Frisian raising diphthongs as a case of shift. Journal of Estonian and Finno-Ugric Linguistics, 2(1), 125–140. https://doi.org/10.12697/jeful.2011.2.1.08
